surprises.description: NBN reported diluted EPS of $3.42, essentially matching the published $3.41 consensus but falling short of the preview’s stated $3.60–$3.75 functional buy-side bar. The preview explicitly warned that an in-line consensus result would disappoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 net income was $29 million, or $3.42 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The functional buy-side bar is $3.60–$3.75, not $3.41. An in-line $3.41 is a disappointment.”

surprises.description: NIM fell to 4.57%, below the preview’s 4.70%–4.80% base-case range and below its 4.60% warning threshold. The call attributed the compression to purchased-loan prepayments and a shift toward lower-yielding originated loans, contrary to the preview’s expectation that NIM would remain relatively steady.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest margin compressed to 4.57% from 4.80% in the linked quarter, driven by purchased loan prepayments and a mix shift toward lower-yielding originated loans.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided NIM to ‘remain relatively steady’”; base case: “NIM 4.70–4.80%”; “Anything below ~4.60% reframes the story.”

surprises.description: Total loan generation reached $534 million, well above the preview’s $350–$400 million base-case volume range. This is distinct from the national lending origination record, which was roughly in line with the preview’s bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total loan generation of $534 million across purchased, originated, and SBA loans.”

surprises.description: The purchased-loan portfolio return was 9.11%, above the preview’s expectation of an approximately 8% yield, with a $5.9 million credit-discount release contributing to the reported return. The release ran through provision rather than interest income under CECL, making it a notable accounting and portfolio-return detail not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $5.9 million release of credit discount on purchased loans flowed through the provision (not interest income under CECL), boosting the total purchased loan portfolio return to 9.11%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The purchased book … still yields ~8%”; management was expected to repeat “approximately 8%.”

surprises.description: Management said about $1.4 billion of CDs maturing within three months are expected to reprice roughly 50 basis points higher, adding about 15 basis points to next-quarter cost of funds. The preview flagged funding costs as something to watch but did not anticipate this specific near-term increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $1.4 billion of CDs mature within three months and are expected to reprice roughly 50 basis points higher, adding about 15 basis points to cost of funds next quarter.”

surprises.description: The quarter benefited from stock-vesting tax benefits, leaving the effective tax rate at 26.2%, while management said to expect a normalized rate of about 29% going forward. The preview did not flag this temporary tax benefit or the higher forward run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The effective tax rate was 26.2% (down from 28.3% a year ago) due to Q1 stock vesting benefits, but management guided to a normalized ~29% run rate going forward.”

surprises.description: NBN reported $1.58 billion of loan capacity without a capital raise and said deployment would require minimal added operating expense. That modestly exceeds the preview’s roughly $1.5 billion capacity estimate and adds a favorable detail on the cost of using that capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The bank has $1.58 billion of loan capacity available without any capital raise, with management indicating minimal added operating expense to deploy it.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Tier 1 leverage was 11.9% at June 30 with ~$1.5B of remaining loan capacity”; the preview identified a capital raise as a concern to monitor.
